blocks.h2: Why Pipes Freeze in McHenry Homes
blocks.intro: McHenry County winters bring long stretches below freezing, and open country lets the wind in.

items.body: Pipes along the top of the basement wall or in a crawl space sit right next to cold air.
Many 1990s and 2000s homes have bathrooms or bedrooms over an attached garage, with pipes in the cold floor.
A seasonal home whose heat fails in January can freeze from top to bottom.
Hoses left connected trap water. Older spigots split inside the wall.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: How do I shut off water if I'm on a well?
items.preview: Turn off the well pump at the breaker and close the main valve.
items.answer: Turn off the breaker for the well pump and close the main valve near the pressure tank. That stops new water from being pumped into the broken line.

items.q: How do I thaw a frozen pipe safely?
items.preview: Open the faucet and warm the pipe slowly. No open flames.
items.answer: Open the faucet, then warm the pipe slowly with a hair dryer or space heater, starting near the faucet. Never use a torch. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: How do I protect a seasonal lake home in winter?
items.preview: Keep heat on and shut off the water, or have it winterized.
items.answer: Keep the heat on at a safe level and shut off the main water when you leave. For long absences, have the plumbing drained and winterized. We can do it.

items.q: Why did my pipe leak after it warmed up?
items.preview: It split while frozen and leaked when it thawed.
items.answer: Ice splits the pipe while frozen. Water escapes once it thaws, so leaks often appear a day or two later.
